    The modular identity for weights of submodules #

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.Weight.eval_of_submodule_quotient {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] {X : Type u} [AddCommGroup X] [Module R X] [Module.Finite R X] (θ : Weight (FGModuleCat R)) (U : Submodule R X) :
    θ.eval ↧X = θ.eval ↧↥U + θ.eval ↧(X ⧸ U)

    A weight on finite modules is additive across a submodule and its quotient.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.Weight.eval_sup_add_eval_inf {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] {X : Type u} [AddCommGroup X] [Module R X] [Module.Finite R X] (θ : Weight (FGModuleCat R)) (U V : Submodule R X) :
    θ.eval ↧↥(U ⊔ V) + θ.eval ↧↥(U ⊓ V) = θ.eval ↧↥U + θ.eval ↧↥V

    Weights satisfy the modular identity on the submodule lattice.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.Weight.exists_largest_weight_maximizer {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] {X : Type u} [AddCommGroup X] [Module R X] [Module.Finite R X] (θ : Weight (FGModuleCat R)) (hfin : (Set.range fun (U : Submodule R X) => θ.eval ↧↥U).Finite) :
    ∃ (U : Submodule R X), (∀ (V : Submodule R X), θ.eval ↧↥V ≤ θ.eval ↧↥U) ∧ ∀ (V : Submodule R X), θ.eval ↧↥V = θ.eval ↧↥U → V ≤ U

    If the submodule weights take finitely many values then there is a largest submodule of maximal weight.
